title: World map: the Equator and the tropics
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y3 lesson 5 (Blank world map with the Equator and tropics (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 5. Colour the tropical rainforests between the two tropics. Label the continents and oceans.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Which continent is the Amazon rainforest in?
questions.model: Find the Amazon on the map. Look at the land around it. It is in South America, mostly in Brazil.

questions.q: Which continent is the Congo rainforest in?
Is the UK in the tropics?
questions.a: No, it is far north of the Tropic of Cancer

questions.q: Core: On a blank world map, draw the Equator and the two tropics, then shade the Amazon and Congo rainforests.
questions.a: Equator across the middle, tropics either side; Amazon in northern South America, Congo in central Africa
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: a red line for the Equator through Brazil and Congo, dotted lines for the tropics, green shading for the rainforests.

questions.q: Extend: Label the continents your rainforests are on.
questions.a: South America and Africa (and Asia if Borneo is added)

questions.q: Stretch: Write one sentence: Rainforests grow near the Equator because ...
questions.a: ... it is hot and wet all year, so plants can grow all the time

questions.q: Big question: why do rainforests grow near the Equator and not in Britain?
questions.a: Near the Equator it is hot and rains a lot all year; Britain is too cold in winter and not wet enough all year
